title: Premise gate
description: Normative contract for the coder-skill premise gate (PRs #946/#947, #1177). Consumers: (1) validates one premise telemetry record from the coder jsonl ($CODER_LOG_DIR/$(hostname -s).jsonl); (2) x-gate-rules holds the normative judge constants -- SKILL.md references this file instead of restating field names or thresholds. Changing x-gate-rules requires re-running scripts/premise-gate-battery.sh before merge.

verdict.description: Scout's premise verdict after the judge confirm-ride (post-softening).

proposed_verdict.description: Judge choice-arm answer. Absent on fallback.

consistent.description: Judge premise_consistent noul (0..1) per x-gate-rules.question. Absent on fallback.

fallback.description: true when the judge was unavailable/failed and scout's verdict stood.

gate_decision.description: What the orchestrator did; lets audits compute firing rate and stop precision.

x-gate-rules.question: Is the issue's premise consistent with this evidence?
x-gate-rules.polarity: predicate-positive -- the dangerous 'yes' must mean proceed, never stop (audit #946 section 5.6; arXiv 2306.08189, 2601.13537, 2509.08480). Applies to every gate below; sub-gates say 'same polarity' instead of restating it.
x-gate-rules.stop_rule: scout falsified/blocked stops only if premise_consistent noul <= stop_threshold; above it, soften to diverges
x-gate-rules.never_create_stop: scout sound proceeds regardless of noul; the judge may confirm or soften a stop, never create one
x-gate-rules.disagreement_rule: noul <= disagreement_threshold on scout-sound = judge dissents; surfaced at presentation, never stops
x-gate-rules.fallback: never fatal: judge unavailable/API failure/{fallback: true} -> scout's verdict stands, log fallback: true
x-gate-rules.telemetry: {stage: 'premise', verdict, proposed_verdict, consistent, fallback, gate_decision} appended to the coder jsonl (SKILL.md Constraint #10); never block on logging; on fallback set judge-derived fields null

citation_gate.question: Is each path:line citation verifiable at that exact anchor in the worktree?
citation_gate.polarity: same polarity; noul here never stops the run
citation_gate.never_create_fail: the judge may confirm or soften a mechanical FAIL, never create one; the shell check is the only FAIL producer
citation_gate.disagreement_rule: judge verdict contradicting the mechanical verdict on an anchor: surfaced at presentation
citation_gate.fallback: never fatal; triggers: judge unavailable/API failure/{fallback: true} envelope -> mechanical check's verdict stands, log fallback: true
citation_gate.claim_support: one batched noul question per report: does each citation's content support its claim? Provider/model/env-var claims (SDK string literals, URLs/endpoints, process.env.* keys) are first-class; grounding sources: issue text, authoritative vendor source, or accepted artifact recorded in a handoff -- junk or third-party-only results do not ground; low noul on any anchor = disagreement surfaced at presentation
citation_gate.telemetry: {stage: 'citation', verdict, fallback, disagreements} appended to the coder jsonl (SKILL.md Constraint #10); never block on logging

plan_completeness.question: Is every externally-observable fact in this plan either verbatim in the issue text or explicitly marked as a grounded decision?
plan_completeness.polarity: same polarity; a confirmed 'complete' means proceed (issue #1107)
plan_completeness.fact_rule: fact passes iff value non-empty AND (source == 'grounded' OR (source == 'issue' AND value verbatim in issue text)); any failing/malformed fact proposes 'incomplete', else 'complete'; absent/empty external_facts proposes 'complete' (vacuous)
plan_completeness.never_create_stop: the judge may confirm or soften a mechanical 'incomplete', never create one; mechanical 'complete' proceeds regardless of the judge answer
plan_completeness.disagreement_rule: noul <= disagreement_threshold on mechanical-complete = surfaced at presentation
plan_completeness.soften_rule: mechanical 'incomplete' softens to proceed iff the judge choice arm answers 'complete'; disagreement surfaced at presentation
plan_completeness.rework_rule: mechanical 'incomplete' + judge 'incomplete' (or fallback) -> gate_decision rework: rewrite 02-plan.json in place (ground the offending facts) and re-run; BUILD never spawns while rework
plan_completeness.fallback: never fatal; triggers: judge unavailable/API failure/{fallback: true} envelope -> mechanical proposal stands, log fallback: true; bouncer has no fallback path (local scan cannot fail open)
plan_completeness.telemetry: {stage: 'plan_completeness', proposal, field_list, judge_answer, noul, fallback, gate_decision} appended to the coder jsonl (SKILL.md Constraint #10); never block on logging failures; on fallback set judge-derived fields null; field_list = external_facts as kind:value pairs (e.g. ['model:sonnet', 'api_surface:maxTurns'])

trigger_exclusions.rationale: polysemous in real plans (data model, identity provider); a hard stop would burn rework on unfixable phases (issue #1125)

plan_completeness.undeclared_facts_rule: warning-level advisory, never a stop: trigger hit in plan text (overview, steps[], recommended_approach; case-insensitive, word-boundary) AND external_facts empty/absent -> gate_decision unchanged, telemetry gains undeclared_facts_warning: true + trigger_hits, and the PR body MUST carry an 'External facts' section stating the plan's external claims or their absence (checked at existing PR-body checkpoints: medium-tier Ship step, CHECK on complex tier); no trigger hit, facts present, or warning acknowledged -> behavior unchanged; recall is partially limited by the fixed trigger list (accepted: a missed trigger leaves behavior identical to today)
plan_completeness.declaration_not_verification: the advisory forces declaration only; declared values are verified solely by CHECK's citation gate

tier_escalation.purpose: confidence-gated escalation on the tier judge answer; uncertainty only moves up the ladder (simple -> medium -> complex), never down
tier_escalation.calibration: measured on 252 non-fallback records (tor-mb-058.jsonl): mismatch 35% at confidence < 0.3, 2.3% at >= 0.9; every low-confidence demote was wrong or a coin-flip; re-evaluate margin vs scalar once ~50 margin-bearing records accrue
tier_escalation.rules: default: choice maps directly (confirm stays; promote/demote move one tier, clamp to ladder). confidence < hold_threshold override: demote holds the proposed tier (gate_decision hold); confirm promotes one tier (gate_decision escalate); promote maps directly (invariant per `purpose`: uncertainty only moves up).
tier_escalation.example: proposed_tier=simple, answer=confirm, confidence=0.26 -> tier=medium, gate_decision=escalate; run the escalated tier without re-litigating
tier_escalation.fallback: never fatal, unchanged: proposal stands with the higher-tier tie-break, log fallback: true; missing probabilities -> scalar rule; missing confidence -> direct mapping; every degradation is a pure function of absent fields
tier_escalation.telemetry: {stage: 'tier', tier, proposed_tier, confidence, margin, probabilities, gate_decision, fallback} appended to the coder jsonl (SKILL.md Constraint #10); margin = top option probability minus runner-up; gate_decision enum: confirm|promote|demote|escalate|hold; margin/probabilities do not gate behavior today -- calibration only
